uniqueness.note: Replaces DC-6. Each physical target contributes exactly one item per class, and the three rows share one View-1 image byte for byte, so neither object identity nor View 1 carries information about the answer. The earlier one-item-per-target rule was the leak, not the guard: it made a target's single class its signature.

presentation.option_policy: deterministic and answer-position-balanced within split/class strata
canonical_options: Visible — It is visible in the current view, either fully or partially.
Out of View — It is not in frame because the camera is not directed toward it.
Occluded — It is in frame but completely hidden by another object.

downstream_release_blockers: S06 independent item-quality and human-verification gate
final release freeze and license authorization
allocation_note: Certified 2026-08-25 (v10). v9 with the visible floor raised from 30 to 300 View-2 pixels: at 30px the 'Visible' label was logically right and perceptually impossible, and every visible-class error a real rater made was an item showing under 300 pixels. 633 sliver rows were dropped at intake; a dropped visible row removes its whole target-matched triple, so the pool is a strict subset of v9 (13275 of 14235 rows) and every structural guarantee is inherited: all rows sit in byte-identical View-1 triples, target-identity oracle exactly 1/3, View 2 unique.
